name: rr
listed_description: Debugger that records non-deterministic executions to allow for deterministic debugging.
reason: No numeric comparison against gdb or lldb reachable. rr README and wiki Related-work page only say gdb's built-in process record has 'very very high overhead (singlesteps the program using ptrace)' (directional). rr's own overhead numbers (under 2x slowdown on application workloads, USENIX ATC 2017 paper 'Engineering Record And Replay For Deployability', arXiv 1705.05937) compare against native execution, not a named debugger baseline, and the paper plus rr-project.org were EGRESS_BLOCKED. Lead: re-check the paper's related-work and evaluation sections from an environment that can open arXiv or USENIX for any gdb 'record full' timing.

name: sierra
listed_description: A CISC-oriented programming language focused on creating maintainable programs.
reason: Sierra is actually a SIMD extension for C++ (clang fork, Saarland University, last activity 2018), not a CISC language. Repos sierra-lang/sierra and sierra-lang/libsierra and the project page source (sierra-lang.github.io index.html) contain no benchmark numbers; libsierra has benchmark sources (aobench, mandelbrot, options, rgb2gray, volume, polybench) but no results files or README. Speedups over scalar code exist only in the WPMVP 2014 and PPoPP 2012 papers, which were EGRESS_BLOCKED (madoc.bib.uni-mannheim.de, sierra-lang.github.io). Lead: retrieve 'Sierra: A SIMD Extension for C++' (Leissa, Haffner, Hack, WPMVP 2014) from an environment with paper access; baseline would be scalar C++ code and auto-vectorization, category would stay compilers-frontends or simd-vectorization.
